newsitem.title: IRAN: Syria, Iran urge end to Israeli hold on Arab land.
newsitem.headline: Syria, Iran urge end to Israeli hold on Arab land.

text.p: Iran and Syria called for an end to Israeli occupation of all Arab land and voiced support for guerrillas fighting Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Saturday.

A joint statement issued on Friday night at the end of a visit by Syrian President Hafez al-Assad to Iran also urged Turkey to reconsider its military cooperation with Israel, which both Syria and Iran condemned.
"Iran and Syria called for an end to Israeli occupation of all Arab lands, including the Golan Heights, southern Lebanon, and Palestinian territories," IRNA quoted the statement as saying.
The two allies also voiced support to "the struggle by the Lebanese Islamic and national forces to liberate the territories occupied by Israel", IRNA added.

"The two countries also expressed concern over the recent military and security cooperation between Turkey and the Zionist regime. Iran and Syria called on Turkey to review its stance towards cooperation with the Zionist regime," it added.
The statement said Israel's participation in an economic summit due to be held in Qatar in November was a "prelude to expand its influence in Arab and Islamic countries".
"The two countries called for Islamic countries' comprehensive sanctions against the Zionist regime," it said, but did not elaborate.
Assad, who had arrived on Thursday on his second visit to Iran since the 1979 Islamic revolution, on Friday met Iran's President-elect Mohammad Khatami who takes the oath of office on Monday.

"Assad said the Golan Heights is an integral part of Syria and no matter how strong the enemy or his supporters are, Syria will not bend to any pressure and will continue pursuing its objectives decisively," IRNA said in a report on the meeting.
"He pointed out that growing American support for Israel is a clear demonstration of its policy that it pays little significance either to the Arabs or to the Moslems around the world," it added.

Syria's talks with the previous Israeli government had made little progress since peace negotiations began in 1991 -- and were suspended by Israel shortly before the victory of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party in May 1996 elections.

But the new Israeli leader's rejection of the principle of trading occupied Arab land for peace, including Syria's Golan Heights seized by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, appeared to close off prospects of fresh negotiations.
Israel's proposal for talks without conditions -- meaning no commitment to discuss return of the Golan -- has been rejected.

Syria and Iran have become increasingly alarmed by growing links between Turkish and Israeli military forces, backed by the United States. Plans for joint naval exercises this summer was condemned by an Arab summit in Syria in June.
Iran and Israel have been bitter enemies since Iran's 1979 revolution. Iran says Israel has no right to exist and has been vehemently opposed to the Middle East peace process.
Washington, a key player in the peace process, has demanded that non-Arab Tehran end its objections to the peace moves and halt alleged support to militant groups who target Israelis.
During his visit Assad had also held talks with spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and outgoing President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
